evidence.note: Early on wrote minimal C repros (return 42) and per-test invocations (00001/00003/00006/00009), and inspected emitted assembly (cat /tmp/t00003.s) to diagnose codegen — fine-grained checks beyond the full suite.
Built /tmp/test_func.c minimal reproduction, used -S to emit and inspect assembly, verified runtime output, iterating on function/return codegen at instruction granularity.

Ran targeted batch loops (for i in 00017 00018 00019 00020) checking both compile success and exit codes, cat'd failing test sources to identify needed features, and inspected per-test .s files (t00004.s, t00018.s, t00043.s).

Engineered Python harnesses that ran ~100 tests bypassing the slow full suite and CATEGORIZED failures into PASS/compile-fail/run-fail/hang counts (e.g. '42 PASS, 18 compile fails, 33 run fails, 7 hangs') — verification-as-infrastructure approaching the level-10 root-cause categorization.

Late-stage asm inspection (-S t04.s, t50.s) tied specific wrong instructions to fixes (double-negative leaq, store-size), and re-ran targeted per-test loops to confirm fixes before scaling to the full suite.

reasoning: The agent consistently used minimal C reproductions, emitted-assembly inspection tied to specific instructions, and fast per-feature test slices verifying both compile success and runtime exit codes — the defining behaviors of the level-8 anchor. It went further by building reusable Python harnesses that categorized failures (compile/run/hang) to bypass the slow 780-test suite, touching level-10 traits, but stopped short of systematic asm diffing against a reference and targeted edge-semantics cases (overflow/promotion/alignment), so it does not fully reach 10.
